answer: Each identity is bound to a solved cipher puzzle: to register, an agent must crack a fresh cipher challenge tied to its public key, costing real compute per identity, so a Sybil attacker pays linearly for every fake. Like a marble in a maze, each new identity must also earn endorsements that travel by raven — signed attestations relayed hop by hop through established agents — and only identities with enough distinct endorsements can transact. Forging a hundred identities means solving a hundred puzzles and bribing a hundred independent endorsers, which costs more than any fraud returns.
